title: Chapter 4: The Official Record
notes: Revised CH04 (The Official Record). Proposed dialogue pending narrative review. Scenes 01, 02, 03 and 05: Voss's meeting keeps the transfer audit and the spatial survey as separate incident files; the junior summary's 'confirmed mapping error' is corrected with the first version kept; Rahman states the clinical boundary; an outside reviewer finds a time-order contradiction that cannot be removed without excluding an original. Scene 04 (optional, owner asked for the content gaps to be filled 2026-10-19): Mara's follow-up in Interview Room A after Rahman's boundary and before the door check, using the screenplay lines only; her care continues and nothing goes into the incident record. New clinical wording, pending the executive producer's review. Scene 06 (optional): a personal call at the nursing station after the paper trail, from the contact chosen at the end of Chapter 2 (partner, friend, family, own reminder, or someone close for older saves); accept support, keep it short or set a boundary; no patient or inquiry detail is shared. The Scene 09 corridor-loop reveal waits for the owner's approval of its effect. Scenes 07-08 (Door-state replication attempt, Institutional disagreement): a controlled, continuously watched check of the lift lobby doors; nothing happens during the watch, and the result cannot exclude an authorized entry between the original checks, so repeatability stays open (no 'corroborated' from repeated logs). Voss, Hale and Rahman agree patient care continues and the restriction stands; the player proposes external verification, a coordinated briefing or documented dissent; safety notifications happen regardless.

objectives.text: Dr Voss has called Hale, Facilities and you to her office area.
An administrative summary is waiting at the office workstation.
Dr Rahman wants a word at the office desk.
The outside reviewer's comparison is on the Records worksheet.
Hale is setting up a controlled check of the lobby doors. Join him at Interview Room A's door.
Watch the lift lobby doors with the team for the controlled check.
Return the test pass to Hale.
Voss is meeting Hale and Rahman about access and patient continuity.
Hale is briefing a controlled inspection of the Ward Zero corridor. Find him at Interview Room A's door.
Go down with the team to the Ward Zero corridor and log the landmarks at the alcove.
Walk the permitted corridor straight on to the junction marker with the team.
Return the team pass to Hale.
Voss is writing the official record at the office desk.
Voss wants one last word on how the inquiry stays honest.

actions.notify: Your phone is buzzing. You can take the call on a break at the nursing station.
Logged: observed repetition, unverified. Both survey sheets come from the same walk, not from independent instruments.

staff_lines.text: Stop word is 'hold'. Anyone says it, everyone stops and we come out.
Lobby doors, the team, a watch that doesn't blink. That's the test.
Different questions, different evidence. Come and find me when it's a clinical one.
Nobody enters pending the independent safety review.
Two incident files. Keep them that way.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: the morning after
interactions.body:
Voss: We are not here to settle a theory. We have observations we can't yet reconcile and a restricted area with possible safety implications.

Engineer: Some old plans are incomplete. Other differences remain unexplained.

Hale: Nobody enters pending the independent safety review.

You: The inactive-credential transfer request remains an information-security question.

Voss: Precisely. Don't join two incomplete cases just because their labels resemble each other.

options.label: Propose one combined W0-B case file
options.response: Voss: No. The transfer audit and the spatial survey are separate incident files until something other than a label connects them.

options.label: Preserve transparent findings in both files
options.response: Voss: Good. Both files say what was observed and what wasn't.

options.label: Focus on the access restrictions first
options.response: Hale: Then we agree. The restriction stays until the safety review signs off.

options.label: Request outside expertise for the survey
options.response: Voss: I'll ask for an outside reviewer. The safety review still comes first.

interactions.title: Administrative summary (draft)
interactions.body:
A junior administrator's draft summary of the Chapter 3 inspection reads: "Cause: confirmed mapping error." No review has established a cause. Facilities' own file says unresolved.

Voss (note): Then the summary is wrong. Correct it. Keep the first version in the revision history.

options.label: Leave "confirmed mapping error" as the finding
options.response: Not established. A mapping error is one candidate explanation; no review has confirmed it. The draft stays open for revision.

options.label: Replace it with "anomalous geometry confirmed"
options.response: Not established either. Nothing the inspection recorded supports that wording. The draft stays open for revision.

options.label: State the observed contradiction and that the cause is unresolved
options.response: Official finding entered: plan editions and observations disagree; cause unresolved; independent review pending. The first draft is kept in the revision history.

interactions.completed_body: Official finding: contradiction observed, cause unresolved. Revision history kept.

interactions.title: Dr Rahman: clinical boundary
interactions.body: Rahman: An unusual facilities report doesn't change the standards for evaluating a patient who is distressed or sleeping poorly.

options.label: Suggest the corridor report might explain some patients' distress
options.response: Rahman: No. A building report isn't a clinical finding, and a patient's distress isn't building evidence. We assess the patient.

options.label: "And an old psychiatric diagnosis doesn't prove an audit record false."
options.response: Rahman: Both are important. Different questions need different evidence.

interactions.title: Mara Ellis: follow-up
interactions.body:
Mara is in Interview Room A for her follow-up appointment.

Mara: Did they decide one of the dates was wrong?

options.label: Tell her the review has worked out which date was wrong
options.response: You stop yourself. Nothing has established that, and giving her an answer the review doesn't have would not be honest.

options.label: "The records differ. The reason hasn't been established."
options.response:
Mara: I wish somebody had said that the first time.

You: I'd also like to talk about how the insomnia has been affecting you.

The rest of the appointment is about her care: sleep, anxiety, how she is managing day to day, and when you will see her again. None of it goes into the incident record.

interactions.title: Outside review: retained originals
interactions.body:
The outside reviewer compared the retained originals after accounting for the known export display differences. A time-order contradiction remains. How independent the originals are is documented, not assumed.

Analyst: I can't make these versions agree without excluding one of the originals.

options.label: Exclude the original that doesn't fit
options.response: Excluding a record to make the others agree would destroy the contradiction, not resolve it.

options.label: "Then preserve them both. Identify which checks were performed."
options.response: Both originals preserved. Checks listed: display-difference correction, clock-source comparison, custody trail. Independence documented per record. The time-order contradiction stands.

interactions.completed_body: Retained originals: time-order contradiction preserved with the checks performed.

interactions.title: Personal call
interactions.body:
You step into the nursing station on a break. Your partner is calling.

Partner: I know you can't say much. I just wanted to hear how you are.

options.label: Tell them about the corridor
options.response: You don't. The inquiry is confidential, and a personal call is not where it gets worked out.

options.label: Let them help: say it's been a hard week
options.response: You say it's been a hard week and leave it at that. It helps more than you expected.

options.label: Keep it short: say you're fine and you'll call later
options.response: You keep it short. A promise to call later, and back to work.

options.label: Set a boundary: work stays at work
options.response: You say you'd rather not talk about work, and that you'll be home on time. They take it well.

interactions.title: Personal call
interactions.body:
You step into the nursing station on a break. No call: the reminder you set for yourself comes up instead.

Reminder (set by you): Eat something. Leave on time. You can't carry all of it.

options.label: Write the corridor into your own notes app
options.response: You don't. Inquiry details belong in the authorized record, not on your phone.

options.label: Message someone instead: say it's been a hard week
options.response: You send a short message to someone you trust. It helps more than you expected.

options.label: Snooze it and get back to work
options.response: You snooze the reminder. It will come back.

options.label: Follow it: leave on time tonight
options.response: You decide you'll leave on time tonight, whatever is still on the list.

interactions.title: Personal call
interactions.body:
You step into the nursing station on a break. Someone close to you is calling.

Caller: Haven't heard from you in a while. How are you holding up?

options.label: Tell them about the corridor
options.response: You don't. The inquiry is confidential, and a personal call is not where it gets worked out.

options.label: Let them help: say it's been a hard week

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: controlled check
interactions.body: Hale: Facilities wants to see whether the lobby door does it again. Authorized test, continuous watch, access logs pulled before and after. You come as the person who logged it the first time.

options.label: Join the controlled check
options.response: Test pass logged: ward entry only, for this check. The lobby doors themselves stay locked.

interactions.title: Restricted lift lobby doors: controlled check
interactions.body:
The doors are closed and latched. The team watches them continuously for the agreed interval. Nothing moves. The analyst pulls the access log and the mechanical inspection notes.

Hale: Can the records establish there was no authorized entry between checks?

Analyst: Not yet. We'll preserve the access logs and mechanical inspection results.

options.label: Mark the first door event corroborated by the second log
options.response: The second log came from the same logging system as the first, and nothing happened during the watch. Two entries from one system are not independent corroboration.

options.label: "Then repeatability is still an open question."
options.response: Recorded: controlled watch with no door movement; an authorized entry between the original checks is not excluded; logs and inspection results preserved. Repeatability open.

interactions.unavailable_body: The lobby doors are behind the ward entry.
interactions.completed_body: Controlled check: no movement during the watch; repeatability open; logs preserved.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: end of the check
interactions.body: Hale: Pass back, please. The restriction stands.

options.label: Return the test pass
options.response: Test pass returned. The ward entry doors are controlled access again.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: access and continuity
interactions.body:
Voss, Hale and Rahman around the desk.

Rahman: Patient care must continue regardless of the investigation.

Hale: The site restriction stands until safety criteria are met.

Voss: We can meet both obligations. What we cannot do is issue a false explanation.

The required safety notifications have already gone out.

options.label: Suggest holding the safety notification until there's an explanation
options.response: Voss: No. Notifications go out whatever we think the explanation is. They already have.

options.label: Propose external verification
options.response: Voss: Agreed. An outside team with its own instruments, under Hale's restriction.

options.label: Propose a coordinated briefing for all three services
options.response: Voss: One briefing, three obligations: care, safety, record. I'll schedule it.

options.label: Formally document your dissent on the pace of the review
options.response: Voss: Noted in the record under your name. The restriction and the care plan stand.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: controlled inspection
interactions.body:
Hale: Controlled inspection, one corridor, one straight walk out and back. Stop-and-return protocol, signed escort roster, an operations contact on the radio upstairs, and a rescue fallback if we lose contact.

Two survey teams. Each keeps its own sheet and its own notes. Nobody copies from anybody.

options.label: Suggest starting before the operations contact is on the radio
options.response: Hale: No. Nobody goes below without someone upstairs who can call it off.

options.label: Confirm the stop-and-return protocol and join the team
options.response: Team pass logged: ward entry, maintenance and the threshold, for this inspection only. Operations contact confirmed on the radio.

interactions.title: A numbered panel
interactions.body:
Beside the alcove, a damaged wall panel: a diagonal crack, and the number 17 stencilled in faded paint.

Engineer: Both teams, your own sheets. Write down what you see, not what the other team says.

options.label: Copy one team's note onto the other sheet to save time
options.response: Engineer: Separate sheets. Copying makes one observation look like two.

options.label: Log the panel on each team's sheet separately
options.response: Logged twice, independently written: panel 17, diagonal crack, beside the alcove. Time noted on both sheets.

interactions.unavailable_body: A corridor alcove. An old radiator under a damaged wall panel.

interactions.title: The corridor that repeats
interactions.body:
The team walks on along the permitted corridor. Straight. No turns.

At the junction marker, a damaged wall panel: a diagonal crack, the number 17 in faded paint.

Escort: That damaged panel. We already passed it.

You: Stop. Confirm our position and use the documented return procedure.

Hale (radio): Suspend the test. Preserve both raw observation streams. Begin safe return.

options.label: Keep walking to see whether it happens again
options.response: Hale (radio): No. The test is suspended. Everyone comes out now.

options.label: Compare the two teams' separately written sheets
options.response:
Both sheets list panel 17 twice, at two different points on one straight walk. Both still came from this one walk.

The team turns and walks out the way it came. The threshold is where it should be.

options.label: Declare the stop condition
options.response:
You: Hold.

Everyone stops. Hale logs the stop condition and the time.

The team turns and walks out the way it came. The threshold is where it should be.

options.label: Request independent analyst review of both sheets
options.response:
Hale (radio): Request logged. Sheets sealed as they are.

The team turns and walks out the way it came. The threshold is where it should be.

interactions.unavailable_body: A wall clock, stopped. A faded junction marker on the opposite wall.
interactions.completed_body: The junction marker. Panel 17 was logged here and at the alcove, on one straight walk. Recorded as observed repetition, unverified.

interactions.title: Marcus Hale: everyone out
interactions.body:
Hale counts the team in: himself, the engineer, the escort, both survey teams, you. Everyone accounted for.

Hale: Test suspended. Both sheets go to the record as written.

options.label: Ask to keep the team pass and repeat the walk
options.response: Hale: No. One walk was authorized. Any repeat needs its own approval and its own instruments.

options.label: Return the team pass and log everyone accounted for
options.response: Team pass returned. Ward entry, maintenance and threshold access withdrawn. Raw sheets preserved.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: the official record
interactions.body:
Voss has both survey sheets on the desk, unaltered.

Voss: Whatever the final explanation, we won't make the discrepancy disappear by changing the wording.

None of this goes in a patient's chart.

options.label: Write that the corridor has been shown to loop
options.response: Voss: Two sheets from one walk is an observed repetition. It isn't an independent result. The record says what we can show.

options.label: Record it as observed repetition, unverified, with both raw sheets preserved
options.response: Voss: Filed. Observed repetition, unverified. Both sheets attached as written.

interactions.title: Dr Voss: keeping it honest
interactions.body:
Hale: Area remains restricted. The original observations stay intact.

Voss: Then the last question is how we keep oversight, inquiry and safety in the same room.

options.label: Ask for an independent inquiry with its own instruments
options.response:
You: An outside inquiry, its own instruments, under Hale's restriction. And patients keep receiving their care without their histories becoming part of the building investigation.

Voss: Agreed.

options.label: Keep the restriction and the safety review as the governing control
options.response:
You: The restriction governs until the safety review says otherwise. And patients keep receiving their care without their histories becoming part of the building investigation.

Voss: Agreed.

sign_out.title: Clinical handoff
sign_out.undocumented_message: Outstanding clinical review still requires an appropriate handoff.
